title: K/DA: Automated Data Generation Pipeline for Detoxifying Implicitly Offensive Language in Korean
measurement_description: The paper focuses on generating and detoxifying implicitly offensive language and trend-aligned slurs in Korean. While it does not specifically measure faith or religion as a primary variable, it includes religion as one of the key demographic categories (alongside gender, region, and politics) used to evaluate implicit offensiveness, identify community-specific slurs, and train detoxification models.
findings: The paper does not provide isolated findings exclusively regarding religion. Broadly, it highlights that models often fail to recognize implicit toxicity or community-specific slurs, explicitly citing the religious slur '개독교' (Dog Christianity) as an example of context-dependent offensiveness. By using the proposed K/DA pipeline to capture such nuanced slurs across various demographic categories (including religion), instruction-tuned models achieved significantly improved detoxification performance compared to baseline models.
